title: DESI DR1 velocities agree with 81% of Gaia DR3 spectroscopic orbits and 63% of astrometric orbits; failures occur at low significance and at periods below 10 d or above 600 d
abstract: Question: do independent DESI DR1 radial velocities (2021-2022) agree with Gaia DR3 two-body orbits (2014-2017 data) propagated with their published covariances? Approach: 3,371 stars of the DESI main-survey backup program have a Gaia orbit and usable per-exposure velocities (1,052 SB1, 275 AstroSpectroSB1, 2,044 astrometric). The DESI exposure zero points vary with an RMS of 4.0 km/s; we tied each of 581 exposures to Gaia with single reference stars (residual systematic 1.30 km/s on held-out controls). For each star we computed Monte Carlo likelihoods for three states: the Gaia orbit, the same velocity curve at a random phase, and a constant velocity. A mixture fit gave class fractions; simulations at the real DESI times and noise recover each state at 92-100%. Results: spectroscopic orbits are 0.81 (95% 0.77-0.85) orbit, 0.16 phase and 0.03 constant; astrometric orbits are 0.63 (0.56-0.70), 0.27 and 0.09. Spectroscopic agreement is 0.92 in the top significance tercile and 0.53 in the lowest, 0.89-0.92 at periods of 10-600 d, 0.56 below 10 d and 0.13 above 1000 d. For 334 well-measured spectroscopic orbits the DESI phase offsets match the Gaia-propagated uncertainty (scale 1.00, 95% 0.83-1.18; 1.6 at 300-1000 d). With a doubled Gaia covariance, 0.95 of the spectroscopic orbits agree and 0.02 show no motion. Per star, 296 spectroscopic and 46 astrometric orbits are confirmed and 8 low-significance SB1 orbits show no motion. Limitations: 1-4 DESI epochs per star within about one month, so 2,203 stars are uninformative; the absolute frame depends on Gaia reference stars; the phase state mixes wrong periods and underestimated errors; astrometric fractions depend on the covariance scaling (constant 0.09-0.21); bright northern stars only.
